concept.name: Overcollateralized loan
concept.definition: An overcollateralized loan is a loan whose collateral value exceeds the borrowed amount — the standard structure of DeFi lending, where borrowers must post more than they take because there is no credit assessment or recourse beyond the collateral.
concept.intuition: Borrow $70 by locking up $100: the lender never checks your credit because your collateral is already worth more than the debt and can be seized instantly.
concept.mechanics: Lending protocols enforce overcollateralization through per-asset LTV caps (e.g. 75-80%) and liquidation thresholds: oracles revalue collateral continuously, and positions drifting toward undercollateralization (health factor < 1) are liquidated permissionlessly to keep the protocol solvent. Interest accrues on the debt, slowly consuming the collateral buffer.
concept.formula: Collateralization ratio = collateral value / borrow value > 1 (e.g. $10,000 collateral / $6,000 debt ≈ 1.67).
concept.failure_modes: Overcollateralization protects only while collateral is liquid and correctly priced: flash crashes, oracle failures or illiquid collateral can flip a loan to undercollateralized before liquidators respond, creating protocol bad debt.
concept.misconceptions: Overcollateralized borrowing is capital-inefficient by design, not a flaw to be fixed by higher LTVs alone — it substitutes collateral for creditworthiness. It also does not make the loan risk-free for the borrower, who can still be liquidated at a penalty.
concept.example: Locking $15,000 of ETH to borrow $7,500 of USDC (50% effective LTV against an 80% threshold) lets you spend dollars without selling ETH, but a ~47% ETH drawdown makes the position liquidatable.
